bank.q: Consider the following statements about India's ADR architecture:
s: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is based on the UNCITRAL Model Law.
The Mediation Act, 2023 overrides the conciliation provisions of the 1996 Act.
Mediated settlements and arbitral awards are both enforceable as court decrees.
bank.e: All three are correct — enforceability as a decree is what gives each process practical force.

bank.q: Match List I (institution) with List II (founding statute or year):
bank.e: The NGT Act of 2010, the Commercial Courts Act of 2015, the Gram Nyayalayas Act of 2008, and the 42nd Amendment's tribunal articles.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The NGT's jurisdiction excludes the Wildlife Protection Act
Only 331 of 4,887 notified Gram Nyayalayas are operational
L. Chandra Kumar removed High Court review of tribunal decisions
The commercial dispute threshold was reduced to ₹3 lakh in 2018
bank.e: L. Chandra Kumar did the opposite — it preserved High Court review under Articles 226 and 227 against attempted statutory exclusion.

bank.as: Specialised forums created to relieve the courts have often reproduced the courts' problems.
bank.rs: Tribunals carry backlogs in the tens of thousands, and most Gram Nyayalayas were never made operational.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the recurring theme across this section.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the roles of neutrals:
s: An arbitrator adjudicates and issues a binding award.
A conciliator may actively propose settlement terms.
A mediator may impose terms where the parties deadlock.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Mediation is purely facilitative — the mediator cannot impose anything.

bank.q: Which of the following is absolutely prohibited under the 2026 draft AI regulations?
bank.e: Recidivism prediction, alongside bail risk-scoring, witness-credibility assessment and black-box systems affecting liberty.

bank.q: All of the following are timelines correctly stated EXCEPT:
o: Arbitration: 12 months from completion of pleadings, extendable by 6
Commercial Courts: written statement within 120 days of service
Gram Nyayalaya appeals: to be disposed within twelve months
bank.e: The appeal timeline is six months, not twelve.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act (1996) → the Gram Nyayalayas Act (2008) → the NGT Act (2010) → the Commercial Courts Act (2015).

bank.q: With reference to judicial technology, consider the following:
s: SUVAS translates judgments into eighteen languages.
The e-Courts Phase III outlay is ₹7,210 crore.
The judiciary has a permanent execution body comparable to UIDAI.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The absence of a permanent, resourced institution is the principal structural criticism.

bank.as: Gayatri Balasamy did not confer a general power to modify arbitral awards.
bank.rs: The permitted grounds are severability, clerical and computational errors, and post-award interest that does not comply with the Act.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Article 142 remains available to the Supreme Court separately.
